note: Swappable grammar pack (R46, §9.3/§9.11) for the DNS line. Machine-checked wall between namespaces: 'decision' strings appear while the player decides or loses (labels, terms, refusals, alerts, status rungs) and stay SOBER per §9.3 clauses 2-3; 'flavour' carries the recognition comedy for quiet surfaces. Authenticity law for this line (§9.3/§9.11): the drama is the OPERATOR's — the candle's draught, the calendar nobody rang, the green dashboard over a dark map — never the attack tooling. No payloads, commands, tool names-as-how-to, or technique instruction anywhere; abuse exists only as complaint, upstream notice, provider silence, and consequence.

nodeId.desc: Board object the decision surface is about (PoP / signer id).

availableAtTick.desc: Tick at which the queued intent or a freed hand presents.

domainName.desc: A customer zone under your nameservers.

ttlSeconds.desc: Record TTL — the pre-committed bet this line is named for (§1.3).

latencyP99Ms.desc: p99 query latency — the candle's number (§7.8 meter law).

popName.desc: An anycast PoP on the world map.

keyTag.desc: A DNSSEC key identifier on the rotation calendar.

rolloverDue.desc: Time left in a scheduled key-rollover window.

queryVolume.desc: Queries per second in a burst, volley, or drain.

victimName.desc: The target whose NOC is filing your reflection complaint.

complaintCount.desc: Abuse-desk complaint count in a conscription tally.

ticketId.desc: Customer zone-change or lockout ticket number.

hour.desc: Clock hour a ticket or volley was filed/observed at.

minute.desc: Clock minute a ticket or volley was filed/observed at.

day.desc: Day of the rotation calendar or the quarter, for the intern's log.

decision.type.dns-hosting.name: The Signpost Network
decision.type.dns-hosting.codex: The resolution line: tiny queries, unimaginable volume, and a meter that reads latency while the real product is correctness. Every TTL you publish is a bet you cannot un-place, the defense runs on a calendar, and when you fail, the failure is silent, third-party, and wearing your name.
decision.goal.dns-hosting.binding: Every TTL choice is a bet: low buys agility and you pay for it in volume forever; high is a mistake that propagates for hours and you cannot take it back.
decision.scarce.dns-hosting.qos: Signed traffic outranks unsigned, and none of it outranks the rollover window — the zone change you approve at dusk is the outage that reads green until dawn.
decision.skin.dns-hosting.inspector: World map at night, pale cyan on near-black — signposts at every PoP, single-frame ping motes crossing to the nearest one, the candle burning in its glass above the map, and the districts lighting up or going dark around you.
decision.cac.dns-hosting.todo: (CAC and time-to-profit unpriced for this line — §6.6 Companion B costs only the shared-web affiliate channel; DNS prices its funnel as free-tier COGS versus the 1.5% conversion race, not acquisition. Placeholder until §6.6 Companion B prices the DNS channel; see bundle _todo.)
decision.economy.dns-hosting.bad-month: An amplification incident originating from you.
decision.verbs.dns-hosting.transfer.1: you are load-bearing for other people; TTL is a throttle you own.
decision.relations.dns-hosting.mastery: The bloom reads the map: PoPs are opened before the tide, not during it, and the complaints thin out when your reflectors are closed.
decision.relations.dns-hosting.distillate: Playbook: correctness is a scheduled asset — rotate the keys like a payroll, answer the desk like a postmaster, and treat every green dashboard over a dark map as a lie until proven.
decision.handover.dns-hosting.runs-out: Your propagation window. A low TTL is agility you pay for in volume forever; a high one is a mistake nobody can un-publish.
decision.handover.dns-hosting.kills-you: A missed key rollover at dusk: nothing is down, everything is unreachable, and your monitoring says green.
decision.handover.dns-hosting.customer-wants: Their domain resolves. Not eventually, not mostly — at every resolver on earth, right now.
decision.rosetta.dns-hosting.rrl: Response Rate Limiting is cgroup caging aimed at repeat sources — the same ladder, now counting packets per second.
decision.rosetta.dns-hosting.allowance: The free-tier query allowance is the oversell ratio in costume: capacity sold to tenants who will never pay, priced against the day they do.
decision.scenarios.dns-hosting.lame-delegation: A delegation walks to a nameserver that stopped answering: a quarter of the world's lookups fail silently, every binary monitor stays green, and the only instrument that sees it is the shimmer of the candle.
decision.scenarios.dns-hosting.water-torture: Random subdomains of a real zone, forever: your cache is beaten, every query comes to you, and the cheap answer — synthesize the negatives — is the very throttle that later starves the customer's new subdomain.
decision.scenarios.dns-hosting.dyn-conscription: You are attacked because of who your customers are: the volley never touches a box you own, it only reads your nameservers aloud, and hundreds of companies go down publicly wearing your name.
decision.alert.candle-draught: p99 at {latencyP99Ms} for {domainName}. No error was returned. Nobody is going to tell you why. The candle leans before the number moves — watch the shimmer, not the value.
decision.alert.rollover-window: {keyTag} on {domainName} is due to roll inside {rolloverDue}. The signer is healthy. The calendar is the risk.
decision.terms.ttl-bet: TTL {ttlSeconds}s on {domainName}: agility you pay for in volume forever, or exposure that outlives the mistake. Every TTL choice is a bet.
decision.terms.staged-publication: Zone changes for {domainName} publish in stages — the validation pass reads the zone before the world does, and the registrar-hijack outcome with none of the villain stays impossible.
decision.refusal.hands-exhausted: Both hands are committed. The {verb} intent is queued and presents when a hand frees at tick {availableAtTick}.
decision.refusal.stamped-in-future: The {verb} intent is stamped for tick {availableAtTick}, ahead of the current minute. Nothing was spent.
decision.refusal.unknown-node: No board object named {nodeId} exists at the current tick. Nothing was changed.
decision.refusal.edge-exists: A {relationKind} cable already links {nodeId} to those endpoints. The existing edge was left as it is.
decision.refusal.slot-occupied: {slotName} on {nodeId} is occupied. One supplier per socket; disconnect before you reconnect.
decision.status.rung-5: We are aware of the fire.

flavour.ticket.subject.new-subdomain-dead: my new subdomain does not exist yet
flavour.ticket.body.new-subdomain-dead: Filed at {hour}:{minute}, ticket {ticketId}. The record is published. The customer's launch was ten minutes ago. The negative cache says it will be true in {ttlSeconds}s, and the customer cannot hear that sentence as anything but an excuse.
flavour.ticket.subject.change-my-ip-now: change the mail server IP right now, tonight
flavour.ticket.body.change-my-ip-now: {domainName} is migrating and the customer wants the TTL they refused to set in spring lowered tonight. The propagation window they pre-committed is the thing they are now asking you to have violated on their behalf.
flavour.ticket.subject.zone-lockout: someone changed our nameservers and we cannot get in
flavour.ticket.body.zone-lockout: Ticket {ticketId}: the account was not breached, the recovery email was. Everything is green and nothing works. The customer's tone has moved past anger into documentation.
flavour.ticket.subject.half-my-users: only a quarter of our users find us
flavour.ticket.body.half-my-users: {domainName} 'works fine' from the office. Your dashboards are green. Their customers in three regions get a timeout. The delegation is lame and nothing you sell currently blinks.
flavour.abuse.canon.reflected: From: {victimName} NOC — a denial-of-service against their infrastructure was amplified using your resolvers at {queryVolume} queries per second. Traffic originated from your address space. They are not suing. They are asking, politely, what your remediation is.
flavour.abuse.canon.abuse-desk: Desk tally: {complaintCount} complaints reference {popName} this hour. Every one of them is about packets you did not choose to answer.
flavour.abuse.canon.upstream-null-route: Upstream notice: your prefixes are null-routed at the exchange until the reflection source at {popName} is closed. Your own map lights stay on. The roads into them do not.
flavour.press.headline.consignment: {hostName} nameservers caught mid-volley; hundreds of businesses down publicly, statements point at an entity none of them chose.
flavour.press.headline.rollover: {hostName} outage traced to an unrotated key; statement calls it 'a scheduled event we mis-scheduled'. Analysts note the dashboard never left green.
flavour.forum.thread.green: Monitoring says GREEN but a quarter of lookups time out — anyone else hosted at {hostName} seeing this?
flavour.forum.thread.draught: The candle moved twelve hours before the alert did. Twelve. We have started scheduling every change around the draught.
flavour.chatter.desk.stack: The abuse desk has {complaintCount} open tickets and the map is calm. That is not a backlog. That is next quarter's null-route, filed early.
flavour.chatter.first-hop: DNS is the first hop. When it lies, every other district lights its own funeral while yours reads green.
flavour.codex.poisoning: The poisoning attempts read as a signpost arrow rotating a few degrees — every resolver that trusts it walks one degree off the map, and the walk is invisible from the post.
flavour.codex.free-tier: The free tier is your only lead source and your largest DDoS magnet, in the same sentence. The product decision is which half of that sentence you can afford.
flavour.loading.tip.throttle: TTL is a throttle you own. Down-trade it now, or pay for it at the worst hour of your life.
flavour.loading.tip.candle: The number is the candle's least interesting property. Watch the evenness of the shimmer.
flavour.intern.entry.calendar: Day {day}: learned the scariest clock in the building is the rotation calendar, and it never rings by itself.
flavour.intern.entry.hundred: Day {day}: every query is worth about nothing and gets one hundred milliseconds. Volume is the whole business. The evenness is the whole product.
flavour.sticky.note.rollover: The rollover was scheduled for a Friday evening. It is scheduled for a Tuesday morning now. — postmortem wall, {keyTag} incident
flavour.vendor.reply.firmware: Have you tried updating to the latest firmware?
flavour.vendor.reply.log-bundle: Please collect a full log bundle.
flavour.vendor.reply.known-issue: This is a known issue, fixed in the next release (no ETA).
flavour.achievement.funnel-pays: Converted at 1.5: The Funnel Pays for Itself.
flavour.canary.pop-drain: {queryVolume}/s draining off {popName} while the bloom sends {domainName} to its neighbours — nearest-wins is a statement about your map, not a compliment.
